hints: Set up two standard normal equations using $Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma}$.
For the second boundary: $\mathrm{P}(X > 102) = 0.719$. Because $0.719 > 0.5$, $102$ lies below the mean, giving $z_2 = -0.58$.
Form the simultaneous linear equations in $\mu$ and $\sigma$, subtract to eliminate $\mu$, and solve for both parameters.
walkthrough:
Set up the standard normal equation for the first boundary:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 121) = 0.20 \implies \mathrm{P}(X < 121) = 0.80$$
From the standard normal table:
$$\Phi(z_1) = 0.80 \implies z_1 = 0.842$$
$$\frac{121 - \mu}{\sigma} = 0.842 \implies 121 - \mu = 0.842\sigma \quad \text{--- (1)}$$

Set up the standard normal equation for the second boundary:
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 102) = 0.719$$
Because $0.719 > 0.5$, the score lies below the mean. By symmetry:
$$\Phi(-z_2) = 0.719 \implies -z_2 = 0.58 \implies z_2 = -0.58$$
$$\frac{102 - \mu}{\sigma} = -0.58 \implies 102 - \mu = -0.58\sigma \quad \text{--- (2)}$$

Subtract equation (2) from equation (1) to eliminate $\mu$:
$$(121 - \mu) - (102 - \mu) = 0.842\sigma - (-0.58\sigma)$$
$$19 = 1.422\sigma$$
$$\sigma = \frac{19}{1.422} \approx 13.361 \approx 13.4\text{ kg}$$

Substitute $\sigma = 13.361$ back into equation (1) to solve for $\mu$:
$$\mu = 121 - 0.842(13.361) = 121 - 11.250 = 109.75 \approx 110\text{ kg}$$
teacher_walkthrough: The weights $X$ of male giant pandas follow a normal distribution $X \sim \mathrm{N}(\mu, \sigma^2)$. We are given two tail probabilities and must determine both $\mu$ and $\sigma$.

Step 1: Set up the first standardisation equation.
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 121) = 0.20$$
Since the upper tail is $0.20$, the cumulative area to the left is $1 - 0.20 = 0.80$.
Looking up $0.8000$ in the normal distribution tables gives:
$$\Phi(0.842) = 0.8000 \implies z_1 = 0.842$$
Using $Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma}$:
$$\frac{121 - \mu}{\sigma} = 0.842$$
$$121 - \mu = 0.842\sigma \implies \mu + 0.842\sigma = 121 \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Step 2: Set up the second standardisation equation.
$$\mathrm{P}(X > 102) = 0.719$$
Because $0.719 > 0.50$, the value $102$ is below the mean $\mu$, which means $z_2$ must be negative.
By symmetry:
$$\mathrm{P}(Z > z_2) = 0.719 \iff \Phi(-z_2) = 0.719$$
Looking up $0.7190$ in the normal table gives:
$$\Phi(0.58) = 0.7190 \implies -z_2 = 0.58 \implies z_2 = -0.58$$
Using $Z = \frac{X - \mu}{\sigma}$:
$$\frac{102 - \mu}{\sigma} = -0.58$$
$$102 - \mu = -0.58\sigma \implies \mu - 0.58\sigma = 102 \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Step 3: Solve the simultaneous equations.
Subtract Equation 2 from Equation 1:
$$(\mu + 0.842\sigma) - (\mu - 0.58\sigma) = 121 - 102$$
$$(0.842 + 0.58)\sigma = 19$$
$$1.422\sigma = 19$$
$$\sigma = \frac{19}{1.422} \approx 13.361$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $\sigma = 13.4\text{ kg}$.

Step 4: Solve for $\mu$:
Substitute $\sigma = 13.361$ into Equation 1:
$$\mu = 121 - 0.842 \times 13.361 = 121 - 11.250 = 109.75$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $\mu = 110\text{ kg}$.
